discovery_question: Do other small landscaping operators share the job-sheet invoicing chore, and would they pay to get rid of it?
decision_informed: Build, keep testing by hand, or stop the invoicing idea.

desired_outcome.metric: Operators who pay for a month of concierge invoicing

statements.text: The founder runs two landscaping crews and writes invoices from paper job sheets on Sunday evenings.
Other owners of small crews lose evening time turning job sheets into invoices.
Operators can be reached through the founder's own supplier and peer network.
A phone photo of a handwritten job sheet holds enough detail to draft an invoice.
Whether other operators have this chore is unknown: no interviews exist.
statements.resolution: Problem interviews or the concierge offer below, after outreach approval.

statements.text: The number of potential customers is unknown.
statements.resolution: Ask for public research approval; no market size is stated until then.

statements.text: Sign-up conversion for the offer is unknown.
statements.resolution: Measure it on the landing page once publication is approved.

statements.text: Whether operators would pay for invoicing help is unknown: nobody has been asked.
statements.resolution: Offer a paid month of concierge invoicing to 10 operators.

opportunities.framing: I lose my Sunday evening turning paper job sheets into invoices.

ideas.title: Job-sheet photo to invoice
ideas.summary: Photograph a job sheet and get a draft invoice to check and send.

ideas.title: Concierge invoicing
ideas.summary: The founder types invoices from photos by hand for a monthly fee.

ideas.title: Crew scheduling app
ideas.summary: Plan crew days and turn finished jobs into invoices.
ideas.reason: Founder declined it: scheduling is a different problem (F2).

ideas.title: Voice-note invoice drafts
ideas.summary: Dictate the job at the site and get an invoice draft.

ideas.title: Accounting software sync
ideas.summary: Push approved invoices into the operator's accounting tool.

checkpoints.question: Which assumptions should be tested first?

assumptions.text: Other small-crew owners have the same invoicing chore and want it gone.
Operators will pay a monthly fee for invoicing help.
A checked invoice back by Monday morning is worth more than doing it yourself.
Operators can be reached through the founder's supplier and peer network.
Handwritten job sheets can be read from a phone photo.
Customers' names and addresses on job sheets can be handled without consent problems.

experiments.setup: Offer 10 operators from the founder's network one paid month of invoices typed from their job-sheet photos.

hypothesis.population: Owners of small landscaping crews in the founder's network
hypothesis.behavior_or_outcome: Pay for a month of concierge invoicing
hypothesis.rationale: Payment is a stronger signal than stated interest.
hypothesis.measurement: Paid sign-ups recorded by the founder
hypothesis.failure_rule: Stop the idea if fewer than 2 of 10 pay within 30 days.

experiments.if_pass: Keep the concierge running and test photo-to-invoice drafting.
experiments.if_fail: Stop the invoicing idea or reframe the problem.

experiments.setup: One page describing photo-to-invoice with a waitlist, shared only in the founder's supplier and peer channels.

hypothesis.population: Operators who open the page from the founder's channels
hypothesis.behavior_or_outcome: Join the waitlist with a business email
hypothesis.rationale: Tests whether these channels reach operators at all.
hypothesis.measurement: Waitlist sign-ups divided by unique visitors
hypothesis.counter_metric: Share of sign-ups that are not crew owners
hypothesis.failure_rule: Find another channel if fewer than 5 percent join within 21 days.

experiments.if_pass: Use the channel to recruit the concierge cohort.
experiments.if_fail: Look for another channel before more testing.

questions.text: May I contact up to 10 operators from your supplier and peer network for the concierge offer?

next_action.action: Draft the concierge offer and landing page; contact and publish nothing until outreach and publication are approved.
